rationale: The five rows the 2026-10-31 measurement resolved, pinned in ONE fixture so a regression cannot move one without failing the others. Four types are RULED (decorates/renders/mixes_in/part_of) and one (`extends`) is IMPLEMENTED but corpus-unexercised (0 of 3,179 `implements` clauses resolves to an inheritance-shaped supertype). Every construct a keyword scan would mislabel is PRESENT here, and each is pinned TWICE: the ruled type is pinned at ZERO by expectRelationshipCount, and the honest label beside it is pinned positive - an `extend type` member is `contains{extension}`, an interface supertype is `implements`, a directive application is `uses{relationshipRole=directive_application}`, the `#import` convention is `imports`, an executable document is an operation symbol and nothing `renders`. Source of the rulings and their whole-population counts: validation/m14/fixtures/graphql/extended-census.json (1,911 admitted .graphql/.gql files, 22 repositories, 2,338,690 nodes, 0 parse failures). Every row below was derived from the fixture SOURCE; the analyzer's output was not consulted.

expectRelationships.note: the `#import` convention IS published - as `imports`, its honest label, not as `part_of`. The part_of row below pins the ZERO separately.
ordinary member containment, beside the extension member below.
THE EXTENSION MEMBER. `extend type Query` continues the SAME type; its member is contained by Query with metadata.extension, not an `extends` edge to a second type and not a mixin.
`extend schema` adds a ROOT OPERATION to the schema symbol - the 95 `extend schema` sites in the corpus are this construct, not a supertype clause and not a member-set composition.

Node is declared as an INTERFACE in this document, so the supertype clause is interface CONFORMANCE. The fixture keeps it an interface deliberately: an object-typed supertype would satisfy the analyzer's `extends` branch (pinned in ontology-heritage-and-surface), and this fixture must be able to read the zero extends pin.

THE DIRECTIVE APPLICATION. It is a `uses` with role directive_application - the declaration reads the directive's NAME. It is NOT `decorates`: the definition at line 12 carries a signature and no body, which is the callable test failing on the composer half.
ledger rule R9: a declaration's type position is `references{declared_type}`, one label per fact.

forbidRelationships.note: an extension member is CONTAINMENT. Reading it as inheritance fabricates a supertype the document never names.

the directive is applied, but its definition has no body: the ontological ruling says an edge would assert an implementation the population cannot witness. The same site is pinned as `uses{relationshipRole=directive_application}` above.
there is no member-set PROVIDER symbol in this fixture - the extension is anonymous and its members belong to Query itself.
the inclusion target is a FILE PATH and no declaration answers it; the construct is already published as `imports`, and one-fact-one-label (R10) forbids a second label.
an executable document selects fields on a type; it does not render a component. The operation symbol is pinned in expectSymbols; no renders edge exists.
